NARRATIVE AND PLANS FOR TYPE 1 ZONING AMENDMENT FOR
2400 W. GRENSHAW STREET AKA 1124 S. WESTERN AVE., CHICAGO

The subject property is a Transit Served Location, as it is situated along Western Bus Corridor. It
is currently a vacant substandard lot with only 73” of lot depth and no alley access. The Applicant
intends to redevelop this property with a new 4-story residential building with 7 dwelling units
and 3 parking spaces located within the garage. The Applicant needs a zoning change to a B2-3
Neighborhood Mixed-Use District with optional variation relief for rear setback reduction, to
allow residential use on the ground floor and to comply with the standards and the bulk
requirements of the Ordinance for this redevelopment project.

Project Zoning Change from a C1-2 Neighborhood Commercial
Description: to those of a B2-3 Neighborhood Mixed-Use District
Use: Residential Building with 7 Dwelling Units

Lot Area: 39° x 73° = 2,847 SF (recorded measurements)

Floor Area Ratio: | 3.0

Floor Area: 8,540 SF (see plans attached)

Density: 406 Square Feet per DU

Off- Street Parking: | Parking spaces: 3

Setbacks: Front: 12 inches
Side: 12 inches on each side
Rear: 9° (see variation request below)

Building Height: | 41°-10” per the attached plans

17-3-0308 Specific Criteria for Transit-Served Locations. In B and C districts, any new
construction within 2,640 feet of a CTA or METRA rail station entrance or exit must satisfy all
of the following specific criteria:

While the subject property is a transit served location as it is located along the Western Bus Corridor,
Section 17-3-0308 does not apply to this redevelopment project since the property is not located
within 2,640 feet of a CTA or METRA rail station entrance or exit. Notwithstanding the non-
applicability of this Section, the project has been designed to substantially comply with the following:

1. The project complies with the applicable standards of Section 17-10-0102-B Transit-Served
Locations:

The subject property is a Transit Served Location, as it is located along the Western Bus Corridor;
however, it is not located within 2,640’ of any CTA or METRA station.

2. The project complies with the standards and regulations of Section 17-3-0504, except paragraph H
if the project is not located along a pedestrian street and except paragraph C if the land use is
designated in a non-commercial use group, pertaining to pedestrian streets and pedestrian retail
streets, even if the project is not located along a pedestrian street or a pedestrian retail street;

The subject property is not located along Pedestrian Street or Pedestrian Retail Street; however,
the project complies with the following criteria:

(a) The entire building facade abuts the sidewalk or is located within 5 feet of the sidewalk.

(b) The requirements of Section 17-4-0504-C Transparency standards do not apply to the subject
development as proposed building is entirely residential (non-commercial use group) and there is
no commercial space which would require clear, non-reflective windows, and the project will not
provide any product display windows.

(c) In substantial compliance with Section 17-3-0504-D, the building will have a primary entrance
door facing Western Avenue.

(d) All off-street parking spaces will be located inside the principal building and will not be
visible from the right-of-way.

(e) The parking area will be located inside the principal building (on the ground floor, per plans
attached). Since the property has no alley access, vehicle access to the parking area will come via
the proposed driveway, according to the site plan attached.

3. The project complies with the general goals set forth in the Transit Friendly Development Guide:
Station Area Typology, and any other station-specific plans, designs or guidelines adopted by the
Chicago Plan Commission.

This Criteria is not applicable to this project.

Final for Publication

4. Residential building projects shall not have a number of. parking spaces in excess of 50% of the
Minimum Automobile Parking Ratio for the applicable district listed in Section 17-10-0208 with
any fractional result rounded up to the next higher whole number, unless additional parking spaces
are approved as an administrative adjustment under the provisions of Section 17-13-1003-EE.

With this proposed redevelopment, the Applicant is proposing a parking ratio which is not in
excess of 50% of the Minimum Automobile Parking Ratio for the applicable district listed in
Section 17-10-0208.

5. The project complies with the Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules of the Chicago
Department of Transportation. The City's Commissioner of Transportation is authorized to issue
Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules consistent with this section.

This Criteria is not applicable to this project.

I. Optional Relief for Adjustment and Variation under Section 17-13-0303-D —

a Type 1 map amendment pursuant to Section 17-13-0300, may include relief available
pursuant to Section 17-13-1000 or 17-13-1100; in such instances, City Council approval of a
Type-1 application containing said elements shall preclude subsequent review otherwise
required pursuant to Sections 17-13-1000 or 17-13-1100, provided that no Type
application permits issued may be in violation of Section 17-13-0310:

(A) The Applicant also seeks relief for variation under section 17-13-1101-B, from rear
setback requirements of Section 17-3-0405-A, which states that for floors containing
dwelling units, the minimum rear setback is 30 feet. To mitigate site planning hardships
on this substandard lot, the Applicant requests a reduction in the required rear setback
from 30 feet required to 9 feet proposed.

(B) ‘The Applicant is seeking all relief necessary, as allowed by the Zoning Ordinance, for
the proposed development per the attached Type 1 Plans.

In support of this request, the Applicant states the following:

1. Strict compliance with the regulations and standards of this Zoning Ordinance would
create practical difficulties and hardships for the subject property, since the subject
property is a unique corer lot, with substandard depth of 73 feet, as compared to the
standard lot in the City which has a depth of 125’; in addition, the site planning hardships
are exacerbated by the fact that the subject property has no alley access.

2. The requested variations are consistent with the stated purpose and intent of this Zoning
Ordinance since this proposed redevelopment and corresponding variations are compatible
with the existing land use pattern on the subject block, which is improved with multi-story
and multi-unit, similar density residential buildings. Furthermore, the new dwelling units
will increase the variety of available housing stock, in response to the growing housing
demand in the neighborhood.
